query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.hypothesis: Simultaneous interstitial doping with Carbon (0.5 at.%) and controlled Molybdenum (4 at.%) in a Co-Cr-Fe-Ni multi-principal element alloy, followed by severe plastic deformation (70% hot rolling) and low-temperature annealing, will stabilize a nanocrystalline (<50 nm) dual-phase (FCC + HCP) structure by suppressing grain growth via C-segregation and preventing brittle Mo-carbide precipitation through precise stoichiometric control, thereby achieving high yield strength without brittle failure.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast Co-Cr-Fe-Ni multi-principal element alloy with limited ductility, coarse grain size (>10 μm), and a tendency to form brittle intermetallics or Laves phases upon microalloying with Mo or C.
generation.intervention: Microalloying with 0.5 at.% Carbon and 4 at.% Molybdenum, followed by vacuum arc melting, solution treatment at 1200 °C, 70% hot rolling reduction, and a short annealing step to refine grains without inducing carbide precipitation.
generation.conditions: Processing under Ti-gettered argon atmosphere; annealing temperatures below the threshold for Mo4C precipitation (approx. <900 °C for short durations); deformation at temperatures promoting dynamic recrystallization but below grain growth thresholds.
generation.structural_mediator: Carbon segregation at grain boundaries reducing interfacial energy to suppress grain growth, combined with a metastable FCC matrix that transforms to HCP (TRIP) or twins (TWIP) during deformation, while Mo remains in solid solution up to the 4 at.% limit without forming Mo4C.
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement is driven by severe plastic deformation and stabilized by C-segregation (pinning boundaries), while phase stability is maintained by the specific C:Mo ratio preventing the nucleation of brittle Mo-carbides, allowing the coexistence of FCC and HCP phases which enhances strength via dual-phase strengthening and deformation mechanisms (TWIP/TRIP).
generation.predicted_outcome: A bulk alloy with grain sizes <50 nm, a dual-phase FCC+HCP constitution, yield strength >750 MPa, and elongation >60%, with no detectable brittle intermetallic phases (e.g., Mo4C or Laves phases).
generation.baseline: The same alloy system without Carbon addition (exhibiting coarse grains and FCC+HCP) or with >4 at.% Mo (exhibiting Mo-carbide precipitation and brittleness) or without severe plastic deformation (exhibiting coarse grains).
generation.boundary: The hypothesis fails if Mo content exceeds 4 at.% (leading to Mo4C formation) or if annealing temperature/time exceeds the stability limit for the nanocrystalline structure (leading to grain growth >50 nm or carbide precipitation).
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty exists regarding the exact temperature window for the annealing step where C-segregation stabilizes the nanograins without triggering Mo-carbide nucleation, as the solubility limit of C and Mo interaction in this specific Co-Cr-Fe-Ni matrix may vary with local chemical fluctuations.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys with 0.5 at.% C and varying Mo (3, 4, 5 at.%). Process all via 70% hot rolling and anneal at 900 °C for 1 hour. Analyze microstructure and mechanical properties.
measurements: XRD to quantify phase fractions (FCC vs HCP) and detect Mo4C or Laves phases.
TEM/EBSD to measure grain size distribution and confirm nanocrystalline state (<50 nm).
Uniaxial tensile testing to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation.
Nanoindentation to assess local hardness and phase stability.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) The 5 at.% Mo alloy shows any detectable Mo4C or Laves phase precipitates; (2) The 4 at.% Mo alloy exhibits grain growth >50 nm after annealing; or (3) The 4 at.% Mo alloy shows brittle fracture (elongation <10%) despite the dual-phase structure.

Question: How do simultaneous microalloying with carbon (C) and molybdenum (Mo) affect the microstructure evolution, phase stability, and mechanical properties of Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloys?. System: [Co40Cr25(FeNi)35−yMoy]100−xCx (x = 0, 0.5; y = 3, 4, 5 at.%) HEAs. Processing: Vacuum arc melting of pure elements (≥99.9 wt.%) under Ti-gettered argon atmosphere, melted five times for homogeneity, solution treated at 1200 °C for 2 h, water quenched, and hot rolled with 70% reduction. Test conditions: Room temperature uniaxial tensile testing at a strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; XRD (20° to 100°, 40 kV, 40 mA); SEM and EBSD analysis.
